blocking.title: The zeroize-chain gate does not run `cargo metadata --locked` — it runs `cargo metadata --format-version 1`, re-resolves on a manifest/lock mismatch and rewrites the Cargo.lock of the tree it audits; four narrations say the opposite and no test covers the spawn
blocking.detail: scripts/check-zeroize-chain.ts:64-67 spawns `cargo` with ["metadata", "--format-version", "1"]; the error string two lines below says `cargo metadata --locked failed`. The same false statement is in ci.yml:42-44 (added by 6d620fc: 'reads the resolved graph through `cargo metadata --locked`'), in the eeffa84 message ('reading the resolved graph (`cargo metadata --locked`)'), in the 6d620fc message ('shells out to `cargo metadata --locked`') and in DEPENDENCIES.md review notes ('reads `cargo metadata --locked` and refuses ...'). Replayed twice: on origin/main with the anchors removed, `cargo metadata --locked` exits 101 (`cannot update the lock file`) while the gate re-resolves, prints `ghash 0.5.1: zeroize MISSING` and leaves ` M Cargo.lock` behind; on mutant M1 the gate rewrote Cargo.lock before the following `cargo check --locked`, which then passed on the rewritten lock. The PR body's evidence line 'Same graph with the two anchors removed: ghash 0.5.1: zeroize MISSING ...' can only have been produced by such a lock-rewriting run — the sentence 'same graph' is not what happened, the graph was re-resolved. Why blocking in the architecture role: this gate is the declared replacement for the retired direct feature anchors (b333b8b: 'The gate is what lets the anchors go'), i.e. the control on whose strength a security anchor was removed; the control shipped is not the control described, it has a side effect on the checkout, and `readResolvedMetadata()` has no test (the five tests exercise `evaluateZeroizeChain` on fixtures only, so a mutant on the argv is unobservable). Exploitability today is bounded: a PR whose lock is stale fails `cargo test --locked` in the required job Rust quality, so the mismatch cannot merge through this gate — the verdict text would be wrong, the merge would still be blocked elsewhere. Fix is small: pass `--locked` (and drop the stale `?? []` comment about it), export the argv as a constant and assert it in check-zeroize-chain.test.ts, and re-derive the PR-body demonstration from the unanchored.json fixture rather than from a live re-resolution.

minor.title: `cpubits 0.1.1` as an exact direct pin has a divergence mode the gate does not cover; the direct `aes` pin's `zeroize` feature is redundant
minor.detail: The width assertion evaluates the `cpubits!` macro of the crate *this workspace* pins (=0.1.1). It equals the width `aes` compiles with only while `aes` resolves to the same cpubits package. A future `aes` bumping its requirement to a semver-incompatible cpubits (0.2) would resolve two cpubits versions: the assertion would then prove the width of 0.1.1 while aes uses 0.2's rule, and nothing refuses that (cpubits is not in ZEROIZE_CHAIN; `cargo deny` bans.multiple-versions = "warn"). The belt already closes this on wasm32 — `--cfg cpubits="64"` is a rustc cfg seen by every crate, cpubits 0.1.1 and later documents it as the override, and the compile_error enforces its presence — so the heuristic assertion is a second, weaker proof. Two options for the owner: (a) keep the pin and add `cpubits` to the uniqueness half of the gate (one line in ZEROIZE_CHAIN-like list, without the zeroize check), or (b) drop the direct cpubits pin and the heuristic assertion, keeping belt + compile_error as the single proof (simpler graph, one fewer exact pin on a heuristic crate). Also observed: `polyval 0.7.3` selects its backend through cpubits as well (`cargo tree -i cpubits`), which the narration does not mention — the belt covers it, the assertion does not. Separately, mutant M2 shows the `features = ["zeroize"]` on the direct `aes` pin is decorative (aes-gcm forwards `aes?/zeroize`); DEPENDENCIES.md lists it as the pin's feature set, which is true but not load-bearing — the direct `aes` pin exists only to host `aes::Aes256` in the assertion, as the crate Cargo.toml comment says.

residualRisks: The `RUSTFLAGS=""` half of the belt claim (49e7314) was not replayed by this pass — the harness refused an env-prefixed cargo invocation; the flag-removal half (exit 101) was.

The compile-time proofs (ZeroizeOnDrop, width, belt) have no second observer: removing an assertion is invisible to every gate (M8). This is inherent to compile-time assertions; a grep-style presence check in the gate script would be the only mitigation.
